thesis: Vertiv is the picks-and-shovels power/cooling franchise of the AI datacenter build-out running at maximum thrust: 252% organic order growth, a $15B backlog, sales +23% with adjusted operating margin up 170bps, and confident 2026 guidance. The stock has rewarded it (+145% over 52 weeks to $333, ~$128B cap) - which is the problem: at ~75x trailing and ~44x forward earnings, the market prices the order boom as a permanent state. Order books this hot (252%) are bullwhip territory: they overstate steady-state demand, and when hyperscaler capex digests, orders mean-revert before revenue does. The -4.8% two-week drift alongside the AI-complex pullback is the first wobble.
catalysts: Q2 2026 results (~late July 2026): backlog conversion and book-to-bill above 1 are the numbers to watch
$15B backlog burning into revenue through 2026-27 - near-term revenue visibility is genuinely exceptional
Liquid-cooling adoption wave (AI rack densities force retrofit demand)
Margin trajectory (adjusted OM +170bps with pricing power intact)
Hyperscaler capex announcements (AMZN $200B, MSFT $190B directly feed Vertiv's funnel)
risk_factors: Valuation: ~44x forward earnings for cyclical electrical equipment; the multiple assumes the order boom never normalizes
Bullwhip: 252% order growth overstates end demand; double-ordering during shortages unwinds violently when lead times normalize
Competition: Schneider Electric, Eaton, and new liquid-cooling entrants target the same sockets with bigger balance sheets
Customer concentration in hyperscaler capex - the same single macro variable as the rest of the AI complex
Coverage vintage: the sourced order/backlog data is from the February 2026 report; Q1 2026 detail was not captured - staleness flagged

organic_order_growth.source: Vertiv Q4 FY2025 8-K coverage (Filing Fool, Feb 2026)

market_cap.note: ~384M shares at 333.05; trailing P/E 75.53, forward 44.02; +145% over 52 weeks
